deviations_from_ac: None at the review level. Three architectural-deviation surfaces flagged at the implementation level (Observations 3, 7, 8) are documented in the builder's marker but not in code commentary; reviewer recorded them for ehp.13's awareness. The DispatchContext shape divergence (epicId/repoPath/contextBuiltAt dropped; epicLabels/stageEnteredAt added) is a defensible design choice but reads of the architecture doc will not match the source one-for-one — flagged as Observation 3 with a suggestion to add a JSDoc cross-reference.
surprises_or_findings: 1. wave:2 label is not present on beads_web-ehp.3 — continues the Wave-1 pattern. The dep-naive start-wave dispatcher reads wave labels at runtime; missing labels could silently exclude beads from being dispatched to a wave even when the plan considers them in scope. Cross-reference: Wave-1 Round-1 Observation 2 + agent-discipline § 2 step 6.

2. Architecture's DispatchContext (line 120-133) has epicId/repoPath/contextBuiltAt fields; implementation drops these and adds epicLabels/stageEnteredAt. Builder's marker enumerates this under deviations_from_ac, but the divergence is not mentioned in code JSDoc. Future readers comparing architecture doc to source will spend time cross-referencing — a one-line JSDoc on the DispatchContext interface ('Field set adapted from architecture § Data Model — see deviations summary') would close the gap.

3. Marker filename derivation: buildDispatchContext reads only <epicId>.json (per-bead markers). The architecture's Seam 2 (action-classifying for marker reads) requires reading epic-scope markers (<epicId>-<stage>.json) for actions targeting an epic stage — coherence's escalation marker is the most operationally important example. Wave-2 documents this limitation in code (lines 502-512); ehp.13 must action-classify per Seam 2 so coherence-escalation markers actually gate downstream auto-progression. The OPERATOR_DECISION_PENDING test cases all use per-bead markers and do not exercise the architecturally significant coherence-marker path.

4. The Validation-Scattered drift-guard test only spot-checks the names array (line 530-545); it does NOT grep src/ for inline duplications of bd-status / operator-decision / review-needs-human checks. ADR-003's 'single source of truth' is enforceable only with a real cross-tree sweep. ehp.13's table-completeness test must deliver this sweep, not just the table-completeness assertion.

5. Fail-OPEN policy for unregistered actions (evaluatePreconditions returns ok=true + warn for actions not in the table) is a Wave-2 transitional choice. ehp.13 is responsible for closing this once the full 38-action table lands. The minimal table covers the canonical 10-action set verified against agent-action-map.ts's AGENT_TO_ACTION — sufficient for ehp.4's load-bearing scope (marker-driven-routing's act() resolves only those 10 via getActionForAgent).

6. The sentinel-typo pattern in the REFUSAL_CODES exhaustiveness test (lines 142-158) is brittle: the comment claims it 'exercises the keys-in-but-not-equal failure mode' but the test maps the typo back to the correct value before comparing — the typo never actually fails. This is dead code wrapped in misleading commentary. Builder's self-review caught this; not blocking.
